clinical_features.symptoms:
signs including HGT, monitor O2 saturation if heavily sedated 
• 
Comprehensive history and exam to exclude underlying medical conditions 
• 
Investigations as per protocol – see below 
• 
Hand over to Psychiatry on call if bloods/vitals/exam is normal 
• 
Psychiatry to arrange rapid transfer to ward as soon as bed is available 
• 
Pts will NOT wait in ED for additional investigations/management unless medically indicated 
• 
Ensure that patient comfort is attended to – toilet needs, regular meals, smoke breaks etc. 
 
 
 
• 
INDEX MHCU baseline investigations 
INVESTIGATIONS 
 
• 
VBG, FBC, UE, CRP, TPHA/RPR (CRP < 60; WCC < 20) 
• 
CSF ONLY if acute meningitis fx OR advanced RVD – Chemistry, cell count, MCS, India Ink, 
CLAT, TB GXP. Add VDRL if TPHA/RPR positive 
• 
CTB if clinically indicated – low threshold for immune compromised pts. With contrast 
preferred 
→ if all normal and no red flags, refer to Psychiatry 
 
• 
KNOWN MHCU baseline investigations: 
• 
VBG, HGT 
• 
Further investigations only as clinically indicated 
• 
Consider drug levels as indicated – anti-epileptics, mood stabilisers 
• 
EXCLUSIONS: Advanced RVD, Thyroid dysfx, SLE, new neurology 
 
ALL FEMALE PATIENTS MUST HAVE A PREGNANCY TEST DOCUMENTED IN THE FILE 
COMPLICATIONS ASSOCIATED WITH ANTIPSYCHOTIC DRUGS 
 
*EXTRAPYRAMIDAL SIDE EFFECTS/ACUTE DYSTONIC REACTION: fixed abnormal posture, oculogyric crisis, laryngospasm 
Biperiden (Akineton) 2.5 mg IV slowly, repeat every 2 minutes prn, max 4 doses 
*NEUROLEPTIC MALIGNANT SYNDROME: develops over 24 – 72 hrs, hyperthermia, muscle rigidity, rhabdomyolysis 
Resuscitate, withdraw precipitating agent, supportive care 
 
RED FLAGS 
* Age > 60 
* Trauma 
* Meningitis features 
* Recent Travel hx 
* Auto-immune/endocrine fx 
* Potentially toxic drug levels – Epilim, Lithium 
* Advanced RVD features 
* Post-ictal features 
* Acute drug intoxication/withdrawal – Medical admission 
* Pregnancy/Recent postpartum 
* New onset visual/tactile hallucination
